steps.what: Capture verified client changes and identify the correct existing client record
Maintain the client database from validated changes without duplicate transcription
Check client database changes and resolve identity or field conflicts

tasks.design: Use a native change form in {CRM} to retain one client record rather than rekeying spreadsheet copies. The manager verifies identity and checks conflicts; possible duplicates are flagged without automatic merging.
tasks.previous_blocker: Client changes may be copied between lists and the central record.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field validation and one authoritative record can remove duplicate transcription.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve identity ambiguity and permitted data scope.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a proposed change belongs to a different client.

evidence.claim: A single client record with native change validation can remove duplicate entry; this design and its time effect are unmeasured.

assumptions: In s1 the spa manager produces verified client ID, changed field, new value, source request, effective date and permitted use; all lookup, verification and capture time is in its 40 hours.
No clinical facts, consent status or marketing permission are inferred; missing authority or uncertain identity returns to manual resolution in s3.
The client supplies the same change request as today; no new self-service capture work is transferred to clients.
Test native record configuration before custom synchronization.
Seven focal and two other-role hours per 100 baseline hours cover field rules, duplicate reconciliation support and access upkeep.
unknowns: Authoritative client system and permitted fields
research_questions: Does one validated client record remove enough repeated transcription to cover maintenance?

already_counted.description: Client lookup, verification and change capture

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65; gross 35 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 28%. Range 0-20% allows uncertain duplication and identity correction; already single-entry databases save zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather staff availability and define demand, qualifications and scheduling constraints
Schedule draft staff assignments within the validated explicit constraints
Resolve staff conflicts and approve and communicate the final schedule

tasks.design: Configure the existing rostering facility in {HCM} using availability, demand and verified qualifications. The manager resolves conflicts with staff and approves the exact roster before communicating it through {CALENDAR} or {EMAIL}; personal performance traits do not drive allocation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Draft assembly repeats, but availability and constraints need reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured shift-planning products can generate constrained rosters.
tasks.still_hard: Handle incomplete coverage and staff preferences fairly.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate workable changes and understand individual constraints.

ambition.what: Recompute draft options after confirmed availability changes, retaining staff consultation.

tasks.altitude: Own service coverage and fair scheduling trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Quinyx supports shift planning; the digest's Barona result is a different setting and does not measure this spa design.
The spa-specific time shares and constrained configuration are unmeasured assumptions.

assumptions: The manager produces staff ID, confirmed availability, verified qualification, service demand, shift duration, rest constraints and preferences in s1; its 35 hours includes consultation, lookup and capture.
Staff provide availability through their current process; new staff-entry work is not assumed free.
Missing qualification evidence or infeasible coverage produces a conflict for s3, never an inferred eligibility flag.
Use native rostering configuration before custom code; validate applicable national employment arrangements and employee consultation during rollout.
Seven extra focal hours and three other-role hours per 100 baseline hours cover constraints and roster support.
unknowns: Local staff arrangements and consultation requirements
research_questions: Can native roster drafts reduce assembly without increasing consultation or corrections?

approvals.approved_version: Exact staff assignments, dates, times, locations and constraint snapshot; any edit invalidates approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75; gross 25 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 18%. Range 0-10% allows changing availability and conflicts; already configured rostering saves zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Inventory products and validate stock counts, demand assumptions and reorder levels
Calculate proposed supplies orders from confirmed counts and defined reorder parameters
Check replenishment proposals and approve and order authorized supplies

tasks.design: Configure native reorder calculations in {PROCUREMENT} after physical inventory and parameter checks. The manager reviews each proposal and orders through {PARTNER_PORTAL}; no autonomous purchase or automatic stock-count inference is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts, pack sizes and reorder levels may require repeated calculation.
tasks.enabler_now: A purchasing system can calculate quantities from explicit replenishment parameters.
tasks.still_hard: Notice unusable stock, demand changes and unsuitable substitutions.
tasks.human_edge: Judge what stock is actually usable and what order is appropriate.
tasks.altitude: Own usable stock and appropriate replenishment.

evidence.claim: Defined reorder arithmetic can generate draft quantities after stock capture; this design and saving are model assumptions.

assumptions: The manager produces SKU, usable quantity, units, reorder point, target stock, pack size, lead time, supplier and current price in s1; its 45 hours includes counting, choosing par levels and all capture.
No par level appears without the manager's demand judgement; uncertain counts or parameters return to manual calculation and review.
Supplier prices and pack sizes come from the supplier's existing catalogue or quotation, checked and captured by the manager in s1.
Use native purchasing configuration before custom code.
Six extra focal hours and two other-role hours per 100 baseline hours cover SKU parameters, price checks and system support.
Purchases remain within existing authority; receipts and invoice processing are outside this order task.
unknowns: Reliability of counts and supplier records
research_questions: Does repeat order arithmetic exceed parameter and stock-data upkeep after physical counting remains?

already_counted.description: Physical inventory and replenishment parameter capture

approvals.approved_version: Exact supplier, SKU, quantities, price, delivery details and terms; changes invalidate approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80; gross 20 minus 6 focal upkeep gives central net 14%. Range 0-10% allows changed parameters and disputed counts; existing automatic reordering calculations save zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain staff responsibilities and service standards

steps.what: Inform staff of responsibilities, expectations, service standards and policies through discussion

tasks.design: The manager explains expectations using current materials in {DOCS} and checks understanding through discussion. No saving is claimed from equating a digital read receipt with staff understanding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy access does not guarantee practical understanding.
tasks.still_hard: Clarify how standards apply in particular client situations.
tasks.altitude: Own clear staff expectations and consistent service.

evidence.claim: Clausematch supports versioned policy libraries and approvals; that capability does not replace staff briefing or establish understanding.

assumptions: This baseline covers explanation and questions rather than policy authoring or a duplicated distribution process.
Use existing document access; no new tool or maintenance workload is introduced.
unknowns: Current briefing process and staff access needs
research_questions: Is repeated document distribution a distinct workload outside required explanations?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Briefing and understanding checks retain full time.

reach: Coordinate instructor coverage with wellness coordinators
